claims.text: Neither of the two behavior changes (the removed ifNull and the new cache) has a test, and the existing tests are structurally incapable of catching either: the test file covering the cache never imports the public entry point with the new caching branch, per-test cache.clear() means staleness can never surface in CI, and no existing fixture event lacks a sample_weight.

`upsampled_count` uses `default_result_type="number"` but wraps its result in `toInt64()` and is designed to replace `count()` which uses `default_result_type="integer"`, causing API response metadata to report the type inconsistently when upsampling is active

What measurement motivated adding the cache — is there a profile or metrics dashboard showing the allowlist's options.get call as a hotspot on the events-stats path? The allowlist option currently defaults to an empty list and rollout hasn't started, so there should be no traffic to have measured yet.

Mark `upsampled_count` as private in discover.py line 1042. Currently it is a public Discover function, so queries can bypass the allowlist/error-query checks and reference `sample_weight` where that column is unsupported.

upsampled_count() removes ifNull(sample_weight, 1), so error events without a sample weight (no error_sampling context, or an out-of-range client_sample_rate) will be undercounted, contradicting this codebase's own parallel fallback-to-1 convention in _get_error_weighted_times_seen.
sample_rate = 0.0 is falsy and skipped

invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code: grepping the whole repo finds no caller, no signal/receiver, and no options-change hook wired to it, so the cache-staleness problem it was meant to solve is never actually addressed.

PR accidentally adds a `sentry-repo` git submodule reference at the repository root (commit a5d290951def) which is unrelated to the error upsampling feature and appears to be an artifact from the development environment
Allowlist lookup is O(n) per project, should convert to a set for O(1) lookups

Column alias is hardcoded to 'count' in transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling, ignoring any existing alias on the column - if caller passes 'count() as errors' the condition fails and upsampling silently does not apply

Substring check 'event.type:error' in query may have edge cases with negated queries like '!event.type:error' incorrectly returning True, or queries with extra whitespace like 'event.type: error' returning False

Hardcoding the replacement to upsampled_count() as count forces the result column name to count, which can cause serialization to look up count() instead and emit 0 for upsampled rows when transformAliasToInputFormat=1 is used
11 lines of trailing whitespace will fail this repo's own pre-commit CI (black/flake8), including one line inside a docstring that black will not auto-fix.

The cache key is built by calling Python's built-in hash() on a tuple, which is unique to this file across the whole repo — the established conventions elsewhere are either readable field concatenation or an explicit md5_text() digest — making the key impossible to reverse-lookup to a project set when debugging (this is a debuggability concern, not a collision risk).

The new cache cannot actually be invalidated: its key doesn't include the allowlist option's own value, so there is no binding between a cached result and the input that produced it, and it can only expire via a 60-second TTL; the accompanying invalidate_upsampling_cache function would need to already know the exact set of historically-queried project_id combinations to invalidate the right keys, and nothing tracks that.
Unused lambda parameter 'args' in SnQLFunction definition for 'upsampled_count' should use underscore '_' to follow file conventions for unused parameters

Is the sample_weight field in Snuba's errors storage nullable, and what is its default? This determines whether F-001's undercounting shows up as a missing time bucket or as events counted as zero, though it doesn't change whether F-001 is valid.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

Several newly added docstrings and comments assert premises that contradict the actual code: a NOTE claiming the allowlist config is always read fresh sits right next to code that just added a 60-second cache for it, a "safe because allowlist changes are infrequent" claim has no supporting evidence, and comments claiming the database schema guarantees sample_weight exists for every event in allowlisted projects are contradicted by the write path.

Which cache backend does settings.CACHES['default'] actually use in production? This repo's own default is DummyCache (a no-op), so whether the new cache does anything at all in production cannot be determined from this checkout.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

The diff adds a "sentry-repo" gitlink (mode 160000) at the repo root with no corresponding .gitmodules entry, which looks like an accidentally committed nested clone unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.

_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling sets normalized_data[sample_rate] for any truthy client_sample_rate without validating the range, allowing values like 0, negatives, or >1 to leak into downstream weighting logic

The stated performance rationale for the new allowlist cache doesn't hold: options.get already hits an in-process local cache first, so this change replaces a single dict lookup on the hot path with a django cache get — a network round-trip against memcached/redis in production — which is likely to be slower, not faster.
Unused 'organization' parameter in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled function

The column-transformation call in _get_event_stats was duplicated into three separate branches instead of being called once before the branching (behavior verified unchanged across all four return paths), leaving three places to keep in sync going forward, plus a newly added alias variable that is never read.
Repeated transformation logic 'transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' in three separate branches could be consolidated
